reliability.label: Reliability
reliability.helpIntro: Your reliability shows how well you honor your commitments when you join an activity. The higher it is, the more others trust you.
reliability.helpHow: Every time you validate your presence on-site at an activity you joined, your score goes up. If you don't validate your presence or cancel at the last minute, it goes down.

badgeHelp.intro: Junto is logistical, not a social network. Two complementary readings to decide on an outing together: the outings you've done and how you come across to others. No overall score, no leaderboard.
badgeHelp.peerIntro: After each outing, your co-participants flag what happened in the field. No written comments, just precise badges — no overall score.
badgeHelp.peerNegativeExplain: Negative signals exist for safety and trust between strangers: better to know before heading out. They stay discreet, only appear after several reports, and fade over time if no new one is added — one bad day doesn't follow you.
badgeHelp.sportsPillIntro: Each sport shows your outings (×N) and the level you declare. The symbol on the right shows your partners' take on that level:
badgeHelp.sportsLevelBody: You declare your level. You can pick a lower one whenever you want, a higher one only if several partners confirm your current level. You judge, they confirm — to prevent any cheating.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: Answers to common questions about Junto. Reach out if yours isn't here.

create.q: How do I create an activity?
create.a: From the map, tap the + button at the bottom right. Fill in the sport, title, date, location and visibility. The activity shows up on the map and in the activity drawer once published.

join.q: How do I join an activity?
join.a: Tap a pin on the map, then the popup, then 'Join'. Depending on the visibility the creator chose, you'll either join directly or send a request to be approved.

reliability.a: A 0-100% indicator based on your behavior: showing up, respectful cancellations, etc. New users start at a neutral level and it evolves with your participation. The more you take it seriously, the higher it goes.

presence.a: On the day of the activity, once you're there, open the activity and confirm your presence in one tap (if you're in the zone). If geolocation isn't enough, you can scan the QR code shown by the creator. Confirmed presence positively impacts your reliability score. If you couldn't validate anything at the time, your co-participants can confirm your presence after the activity.

transport.a: In the Organization tab of an activity, declare your transport mode. If you offer car seats, other participants can request one. You can accept or decline. A private conversation opens automatically to finalize details.

gear.q: How does the gear section work?
gear.a: Everyone can list what they bring from the sport catalog or as free text. The aggregated summary avoids duplicates, and the per-person view shows who brings what.

report.q: How do I report inappropriate behavior?
report.a: From a user's public profile, tap the three dots then 'Report'. Reports are confidential and reviewed by the team.

delete.q: How do I delete my account?
delete.a: From settings, at the very bottom, tap 'Delete my account'. Deletion is permanent and erases all your personal data. Past activities remain visible but anonymized.

levels.a: You declare your own level in each sport (beginner to expert), from your profile. After your outings, your partners say whether they find it accurate or overstated. You can go down whenever you want; to move up, several partners must have confirmed your current level. It's a trust cue for going out safely, not a score.

badges.q: What do the 'Their partners say' badges mean?
badges.a: After each outing, your co-participants flag your attitude in the field with precise badges (punctual, prepared, accommodating, cautious…). No written comments, no overall score. Negative signals exist for safety between strangers: they stay discreet and fade over time if no new one is added.

leave.q: How do I leave or cancel an activity?
leave.a: As a participant, open the activity and tap 'Leave activity': it has no impact on your reliability, except within 12 hours of the start — the creator can then waive the penalty. As the creator, you can 'Cancel the activity': all participants are notified with your reason.

messaging.q: How do I chat with others?
messaging.a: Two spaces. The activity wall, visible to participants, for everything about the outing. And private messages: from someone's profile you send a contact request; once accepted, the conversation opens. Private messaging also opens automatically when you coordinate a carpool.

alerts.q: How do I get notified about new activities?
alerts.a: Create an alert: pick a zone, a sport, a level and a date range. You'll get a notification as soon as a matching activity is created near you. You can have up to 10 alerts, managed from the Alerts tab on the map.

block.q: How do I block a user?
block.a: From someone's public profile, tap the three dots then 'Block this user'. You'll no longer see their activities or messages. You can unblock them anytime in the same place.

pro.q: What is a Pro profile and an offering?
pro.a: Some professionals (guides, instructors, clubs…) have a Pro profile and offer guided services, shown on the map with a dedicated pin. You can view their offerings, their details and the reviews left by other participants.

peerDesc.punctual: Shows up on time at meeting points, doesn't keep the group waiting.
peerDesc.prepared: Has the right gear, knows the route, doesn't improvise.
peerDesc.conciliant: Adapts to the group's pace, doesn't impose.
peerDesc.prudent: Manages risk soundly, doesn't push past safety limits.
peerDesc.unprepared: Showed up without the necessary gear or preparation — the group had to adapt.
peerDesc.aggressive: Aggressive or disrespectful behavior toward other participants.
peerDesc.reckless: Reckless decisions that put the group at risk or ignored safety signals.
peerDesc.level_over: Stated level was higher than the actual level on the activity.
peerDesc.level_right: Stated level matched the actual level.
peerDesc.level_under: You were actually more comfortable than your stated level.
